This is a group project I worked on. It was a very free form project where we were really allowed to do whatever we wanted which I beleive allowed my group to create something that I am truely proud of
       . For the project we wanted to create a terrain a world generator for dungeons and dragons campagins. I need to state that I am not really a huge dungeons and dragons person
       but I am a really big fan of terrain genertaions so that was the appeal for me. It was a project that I could instantly tell that I wanted to work on.

       There were three main parts of the project that actually needed to be adressed. One was the basic terrain generation for that we really didnt do anything complicated and just opted for a simple perlin noise generation algorthm.

       Next we wanted however to generate water features such as lakes and rivers.

       This was a little more complicated and we used a greedy search algorithm. We choose a greedy search algorithm because if you think about it water flows kinda like a greedy search where it just follows gravity and all leaves from whatever hole that it can find.

       Finally we had the part of the project that I was in charge of which was generating the roads. This was my part of the project and I used an A* algorithm roads are made by people who have complicated thought processes when they build things. BUT at the end of the day 90% of the time when someone creates something like a road they are just trying to connect two points in the cheapest and most efficent way. And so with a A* algorthim I was able to accomplish this in the most simple way possible

       WHAT IS A GREEDY AND WHAT IS A*

       A greedy algorithm is a algorithm that at each step takes the cheapest choice without consideration for what is next

       A* Search is an informed search algorithm that uses heuristics to guide its search towards the goal more efficiently than a simple greedy algorithm.

       Greed First Search
       Looks for the greatest negative change in elevation
       Pools up a local minimums, then creates offshoot rivers
       Terminates at Oceans

       A* Search
       Forms shortest distance link between cities
       Water heuristic
       Elevation heuristic
       Distance heuristic:
       (△x+△y)-min(△x, △y)
       Cost uses the same functions for all nodes up to the current point
